random-variable.def: A quantity whose value is uncertain until observed; ISLP writes it as a capital letter, \(X\).

pmf.def: For a discrete variable, \(p(k)=\Pr(X=k)\); the values add to 1.

pdf.def: For a continuous variable, the curve whose area between \(a\) and \(b\) is \(\Pr(a\le X\le b)\); total area 1.

variance.def: \(\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb{E}[(X-\mu)^2]=\mathbb{E}[X^2]-\mu^2\); its square root is the standard deviation.

covariance.def: \(\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb{E}[(X-\mu_X)(Y-\mu_Y)]\); divided by both SDs it gives the correlation.

normal-distribution.def: The bell curve \(N(\mu,\sigma^2)\); 68%, 95%, 99.7% of the area within 1, 2, 3 SDs.

independence.def: \(\Pr(A,B)=\Pr(A)\Pr(B)\): knowing one tells you nothing about the other.

bayes-rule.def: \(\Pr(A\mid B)=\Pr(B\mid A)\Pr(A)/\Pr(B)\): posterior = likelihood × prior / evidence.

likelihood.def: The probability of the observed data, viewed as a function of the parameters.

mle.def: The parameter value that makes the observed data most probable: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_\theta \log L(\theta)\).

standard-error.def: The standard deviation of an estimate across repeated samples; for a mean, \(\sigma/\sqrt n\).

clt.def: The mean of \(n\) iid draws is approximately normal with mean \(\mu\) and SD \(\sigma/\sqrt n\) for large \(n\).

confidence-interval.def: A range built so that, over repeated samples, it contains the true value a stated fraction (e.g. 95%) of the time.

hypothesis-test.def: Assume a null hypothesis, compute a test statistic, and reject the null if the p-value is below \(\alpha\).
